title: Dissolve linux_configuration/scripts/ and single_use/ to satisfy the depth-2 cap
objective: Flatten the largest source of directory-depth violations. scripts/ and single_use/ were three levels of pure taxonomy carrying no information, and a 2-directory cap leaves no room for them. Categories move up to sit directly under linux_configuration/, which is what makes the cap satisfiable at all.
acceptance_criteria: linux_configuration/scripts/ no longer exists; its children sit one level under linux_configuration/.
Every relative `source` of a shared library resolves from its file's NEW location, checked by resolving each path on disk rather than by reading the diff.
Every REPO_ROOT derivation that walks up a fixed number of levels is recomputed for the new depth.
All lib/tests suites that passed before still pass, and any that fail are proven to fail identically in the pre-move baseline worktree.
The repo-wide pytest gate still reports 100% coverage.
Every symlink in $HOME pointing into the moved tree is repointed, and the i3blocks scripts are RUN to prove the status bar still works.
No config, workflow, allowlist or ignore rule names a path that no longer exists.
The .gitignore rules protecting untracked secrets still match after their paths change.
out_of_scope: periodic_background/digital_wellbeing and hosts, deferred while the guard-lib repoint is pending; they keep their depth violations for now.
Deduplicating the two Nextcloud implementations, which is a separate change.
Wiring the depth gate, which lands only once the tree conforms.
verifier: check_directory_depth.sh --all falls 248 -> 139; every '$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/...' source resolves on disk; 8 of 9 lib/tests run_all.sh pass with the ninth proven to need the jail at baseline too; pytest_changed_packages.py reports 1798 passed at 100%; find ~ -xtype l finds no broken link; the i3blocks scripts emit real output.
